Sports.title: Sheffield Wednesday forward Harry Gray forced off with head injury after nasty fall
Sports.content:
Sheffield Wednesday forward Harry Gray forced off with head injury after nasty fall

Sheffield Wednesday's Harry Gray suffered a head injury on Tuesday night after a nasty fall during their clash with Wolves.

Gray had to be treated by medical staff and was eventually substituted after appearing to hit his head on the floor.



2 Gray suffered a nasty injury against Wolves in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday Credit: Getty

The 17-year-old forward, who is on loan at Hillsborough from Leeds, was reported to be responsive following the incident.

He suffered the injury in the final five minutes of the Carabao Cup second-round match that Wolves won 2-0.

Journalist for the Sheffield Star, Alex Miller, wrote on X: "Harry Gray has been taken off with a head injury.



"[He] landed awkwardly and bashed his head on the floor, I think.

"He seemed to be responsive and okay, but medics were absolutely right to take swift precautions."

In reaction, one Sheffield Wednesday fan posted: "The way he walked off did not look very good at all, hope he's alright."



Another said: "He's been promising.... hope the lad's okay."

Owls manager Henrik Pedersen then revealed that there is a chance Gray's injury could be a broken nose.

He said post-match: "We don't know if the nose is broken, but we should take him out and let's see."



Sheffield Wednesday out of the cup

Sheffield Wednesday lost Gray, brother of Tottenham's Archie Gray, in the final moments of their Carabao Cup defeat to Wolves.

2 Sheffield Wednesday were knocked out of the cup by Wolves in the second round Credit: Getty

The League One outfit were beaten 2-0 by their Championship opponents after an own goal by Sil Swinkels and a first-half stoppage-time finish from Saheed Olangunju.

Pedersen's side have had a mixed start to the new campaign, having been relegated to the third tier last season.



They won their Carabao Cup first round tie against Bolton and then their League One opener against Leyton Orient, but went on to lose at home to Bradford last Thursday evening.

And now, after defeat to Wolves, they've now lost a second consecutive game at Hillsborough.

Next up for the Owls is another home game, this time against Bromley, who they will hope to beat to return to winning ways.

Sheffield Wednesday won't want Gray to be missing, as he has started every game of the season so far for them.

Sports.title: Celtic out of Champions League as they blow 4-0 aggregate lead in ‘one of the worst results in club’s history’
Sports.content:
Celtic out of Champions League as they blow 4-0 aggregate lead in ‘one of the worst results in club’s history’

Celtic's Champions League aspirations have been dashed in the most humiliating of fashions.

The Hoops lost their Champions League play-off tie to LASK 5-4 on aggregate after the Austrian outfit won the second leg 5-1.

3 LASK overcame a four-goal deficit to eliminate Celtic from the Champions League play-offs Credit: Getty

To make matters worse for Celtic, they scored the opening goal in Tuesday's encounter, meaning they boasted a four-goal lead on aggregate.

Yet that was still not enough of a cushion as LASK levelled the contest in normal time before Samuel Adeniran scored the all-important fifth goal on the night in extra time.

LASK could have had a sixth on the night when they won a penalty with five minutes remaining, but Adeniran - who would have had a hat-trick if he scored - had his effort stopped by Viljami Sinisalo.

The result marks the second-straight season the Hoops have fallen in the Champions League play-offs, meaning they will yet again drop into the Europa League.

Adding extra salt into the wounds of Celtic following the loss to LASK is the money they have left on the table.

Had they beaten LASK and qualified for the league phase of the Champions League, the Hoops would have landed a guaranteed £16million pay day.

Instead, teams who compete in the league phase of the Europa League stand to make a guaranteed £3.7m.

Jamie O'Hara and Jason Cundy react to Celtic's embarrassing loss

Upon hearing LASK had taken the lead on aggregate, talkSPORT's Sports Bar co-hosts Jason Cundy and Jamie O'Hara could not believe what had unfolded in Austria.

"What are Celtic doing? Disaster," O'Hara said when LASK's decisive goal went in.

"What are they doing? How can you lose a game when you're winning 4-0? That'll cost them a fortune... one of the worst results in Celtic's history," O'Hara added at full time.

3 Celtic will now compete in the Europa League for a second-straight season Credit: Getty

"This is one of the biggest disasters in Celtic's history," Sports Bar co-host Cundy added.

What did Celtic captain Callum McGregor say about the loss to LASK?

Hoops skipper Callum McGregor was equally stunned at how his side threw away a spot in this season's Champions League.

Speaking after the contest, McGregor admitted Celtic 'got what we deserved'.

"We looked scared to go and win the game," McGregor added.

"To be honest I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either and kind of got away with it.

"When you play like that, you can't have any excuse whatsoever.

3 O'Neill watched his side capitulate in real time against LASK Credit: Getty

"We apologise to our supporters and the club because there is no way we should lose that game."

When do Celtic play next?

Celtic will look to put Tuesday's nightmare behind them when they return to action against Falkirk.

Martin O'Neill's side have won their opening two Scottish Premiership fixtures while Falkirk have drawn once and lost once.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and possessing laughing gas after car crash
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving and possessing laughing gas after car crash

Raheem Sterling is at risk of jail time after he was charged with dangerous driving by police.

The former Chelsea winger was also charged with possession of laughing gas and failing to provide a specimen following a car crash in May.

3 Sterling was last on the books of Dutch club Feyenoord Credit: Getty

Sterling's Lamborghini was seen swerving across the M3 by concerned motorists, who immediately called police.

He was subsequently arrested near an interchange just outside of Farnborough.

Police statement on Raheem Sterling

A Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.

“No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.

“Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September.”

If Sterling is convicted of dangerous driving, he could face up to two years in prison.

Laughing gas, also known as hippy crack, was declared illegal in November 2023.

Repeat serious users of the class C controlled substance can also face up to two years in prison, while dealers of the drug could be jailed for up to 14 years.

3 Sterling will learn his fate over a car accident in September Credit: Getty

Raheem Sterling's career at a glance

Sterling is currently a free agent after he departed Dutch club Feyenoord at the end of the 2025/26 season.

The 31-year-old made just eight appearances for Feyenoord, failing to score and registering just one assist.

Sterling moved to the Eredivisie outfit after Chelsea terminated his contract last January a whopping 18 months ahead of schedule.

Prior to Sterling's exit, he had not featured for the Blues since May 2024 having spent the 2024/25 season on loan at Arsenal.

Sterling joined Chelsea from Manchester City for £50million in the summer of 2022 but struggled to live up to his price tag, registering just 19 goals and 15 assists in 81 games for the west London side.

His attacking output was a marked decline from the numbers he put up throughout his time at City, where he won four Premier League titles, five Carabao Cups and the FA Cup.

3 Sterling played the best football of his career under Pep Guardiola Credit: Getty

During his seven-year stay at the Etihad Stadium, Sterling scored 131 goals and provided 87 assists in 339 appearances across all competitions.

Sterling's best campaign for City came in the 2018/19 season, as he achieved 27 goal contributions in the Premier League.

The 31-year-old's exploits that season earned him the Football Writers' Association's Footballer of the Year award, the PFA Young Player of the Year award and a spot in the PFA's Premier League Team of the Year.

Sports.title: Swansea City in talks to sign World Cup captain in shock £3m transfer
Sports.content:
Swansea City in talks to sign World Cup captain in shock £3m transfer

Swansea City are reportedly closing in on Porto midfielder Stephen Eustaquio.

According to Sky Sports, the Swans could land the Canada international for just north of £3million.



2 Eustaquio's club career has spanned Portugal, Mexico and the US Credit: Getty

The report adds Porto hope to insert a 10 per cent sell-on clause into the deal.

Eustaquio has made over 150 appearances for the Portuguese giants since he joined in January 2022.

However, he started just four times for Porto last term before joining Major League Soccer outfit Los Angeles FC in January.



And having moved into the final year of his contract, Porto are prepared to allow the 29-year-old to move on.

How did Stephen Eustaquio perform with Canada at the World Cup?

Eustaquio would join Swansea off the back of the World Cup, where he captained Canada in four of their five matches at the tournament.



The midfielder also scored the winner for the co-hosts in the round of 32 as they beat South Africa 1-0.

Canada's World Cup journey came to an end in the following stage as they were defeated 3-0 by Morocco.



Swansea's pursuit of Eustaquio comes as they attempt to strengthen in central midfield following the sale of Ethan Galbraith to Championship rivals Stoke City.

The Swans will also look for defensive reinforcements after centre-back Cameron Burgess ruptured his Achilles in the first game of the 2026/27 campaign.

What has Swansea boss Vitor Matos said about the club's transfer plans?

When asked about Swansea's transfer plans with just days to go before the window shuts, manager Vitor Matos replied: "I saw the Porto manager said something two or three weeks ago that the market is now like a chess game.

2 Matos' side don't appear to be done in the window just yet Credit: Getty



"I will say it is a chess game in the middle of a storm. So let's see how it goes. I don't know."

And when pressed as to how well Swansea were doing in that chess game, Matos said: "It's still not check-mate."

Which players have joined Swansea this summer?

To date, the Swans have added Stephen Welsh, Elijah Just, Joseph Opoku, Moussa Yeo and Ross Stewart this summer.

Left-back Tiago Parente has also joined on loan from Benfica.

The Swans have enjoyed an unbeaten start to the new Championship season, beating Stoke and securing a scoreless draw against Sheffield United.



Matos' side will look to maintain their unblemished record when they travel to Derby County on Saturday, with kick-off scheduled for 12:30pm.

Sports.title: Wrexham agree deal to re-sign Man City player in £2m deal
Sports.content:
Wrexham have agreed a £2million fee with Manchester City to sign Issa Kabore, talkSPORT understands.

Kabore's imminent arrival means a return to familiar surroundings given he spent last season on loan with the Welsh club.

2 Kabore has been on Manchester City's books for just over six years Credit: Getty

The 25-year-old made 32 appearances across all competitions for Wrexham, registering eight assists.

Although Kabore will join from City, he has never played a competitive fixture for the club since joining in July 2020 from Belgian club KV Mechelen.

Instead, the right-back has been sent out on loan seven times.

Kabore also has 55 caps for Burkina Faso.

Who else has Wrexham signed this summer?

Once the deal is complete, Kabore will become Wrexham's fourth signing this summer.

Danny Imray was the first to arrive, moving from Crystal Palace.

The right-sided player has already made three appearances for Wrexham and even scored the equaliser in a 1-1 draw against Watford last weekend.

Ben Whiteman was the next to join, although he made the switch from Preston North End in controversial circumstances.

The 30-year-old, who was captain of Preston, informed the club he'd played his last game for them in a bid to push through a move to Wrexham, with his actions being blasted by former manager Paul Heckingbottom.

Wrexham then added goalkeeper Anthony Patterson from Sunderland for £8m.

2 Kabore enjoyed a bright start to life at Wrexham, producing three assists in his first two league games Credit: Getty

Patterson joined having been ousted as the Black Cats' starting glovesman following the arrival of Robin Roefs.

The trio of new faces, who will become a quartet once Kabore comes through the door, will be tasked with getting Wrexham into the Championship play-offs.

Phil Parkinson's side came agonisingly close to doing so last term as they finished seventh and only two points off the play-off positions.

However, the Welsh side, along with their rivals, will have a better chance of qualifying for the all-important tournament as this season marks the first campaign with a new-look play-off format.

Previously, the play-offs were comprised of teams who finished third, fourth, fifth and sixth.

But the English Football League has expanded it to include the teams that finish seventh and eighth as part of a major revamp.

Wrexham, who have drawn both of their opening Championship fixtures, return to action on Friday as they host Birmingham City, with kick-off scheduled for 8pm.

Sports.title: National League star says he’s ‘ready for the next challenge’ after club rejects record offer
Sports.content:
National League star says he’s ‘ready for the next challenge’ after club rejects record offer

Boreham Wood forward Abdul Abdulmalik believes he is 'capable of reaching the top' as he issued an impassioned plea to join Djurgarden.

The Swedish club recently had a £1.5million bid for the 23-year-old rejected by Boreham Wood.

2 Abdulmalik is ready to call Stockholm his new home Credit: Getty

Had the offer been accepted, it would have broken the record for an outgoing transfer from the National League.

The current record was set in 2012 when Leicester City forked out £1m to sign Jamie Vardy from Fleetwood Town.

Although Boreham Wood chairman Danny Hunter was hailed by Peterborough United owner Darragh MacAnthony for his 'cojones' in rejecting Djurgarden's advances thus far, Abdulmalik has now voiced his desire to make a life-changing move in a post on Instagram.

What did Abdul Abdulmalik say in his statement?

"Through sheer hard work and perseverance, the opportunity to progress has come around," Abdulmalik wrote.

"This is my chance to push myself as a footballer, elevate my game and most importantly fulfil my promise to the ones around me.

"Opportunities like this are rare, especially within the National League where some of the hardest working talent is overlooked. The game of football is forever changing and decisions are fast paced. There's no guarantee that the same chances come knocking twice.

"I owe it to myself and the kids growing up just like me to fight for this one I've been offered.

"Moving on from a club is one of the toughest decisions in a footballer's career. I'm more than grateful for everyone that has been a part of my journey so far.

"Everyone at Boreham Wood FC and the incredible fans have played a massive part. You will always have my respect.

"With this said, I'm ready for the next challenge. I'm ready to prove to myself and those around me that I'm capable of reaching the top."

2 The 23-year-old has made just shy of 100 appearances for Boreham Wood since he joined Credit: Getty

How did Abdul Abdulmalik perform for Boreham Wood last season?

Djurgarden's interest in Abdulmalik comes on the back of the 23-year-old registering 17 goals and ten assists last season for Boreham Wood.

His goal contributions could not fire the club into League Two as they were beaten in the National League play-off final by Rochdale on penalties.

He was not involved in Boreham Wood's National League clash against Forest Green last weekend, which saw Boreham Wood win 3-0.

He did play in their first two league matches, though, scoring once and getting two assists during showdowns against Tamworth and FC Halifax Town.

Following the match, Boreham Wood boss Luke Garrard effectively issued a hands-off warning to Djugarden by declaring Abdulmalik 'is our player'.

The 23-year-old joined the Hertfordshire outfit in 2024 as a free agent after being released by Millwall, where he rose through their academy ranks.

Abdulmalik also has three appearances for England's Under-17s, where he played alongside Jamal Musiala, Omari Hutchinson and Jarell Quansah.

Sports.title: Chelsea will not challenge Arsenal for the title due to glaring problem, it’s not just Robert Sanchez
Sports.content:
Chelsea will not challenge Arsenal for the title due to glaring problem, it’s not just Robert Sanchez

Chelsea have the capacity to beat Arsenal in a single game, but lack the stamina over 38 matches to challenge for the title.

This is the view of the talkSPORT Breakfast panel with Chelsea told it's not just their goalkeeping problem holding them back from a first league title in a decade.



3 The defensive trio made their first appearance together in a 3-2 win at Craven Cottage Credit: Getty

Morgan Rogers scored on his competitive debut against Fulham at Craven Cottage as Xabi Alonso's side secured a hard-fought 3-2 victory.

The Blues opened up the scoring after just 31 seconds after Joao Pedro slotted home the club's first goal of the new campaign.

The attacking trio of Cole Palmer, Rogers, and Pedro provided a devastating frontline display for the home fans.



However, Chelsea's defensive frailties raised immediate concerns—particularly regarding goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose error directly contributed to Fulham's first goal, scored by Josh King.

Following the match, Alonso said his front three needed to 'lead the rest' so that the 'other ones will follow'.



However, Jeff Stelling told talkSPORT Breakfast that the blame can not only be placed on the man between the sticks.

He said: "It's not just Robert Sanchez. They look lovely going forward. But as I mentioned a moment or two ago, Fulham really should have got something out of that game.



"Antonee Robinson is through one-on-one with Sanchez. Lobs the ball, I was going to say wide, but it's so far wide. They had chances and that was the problem.

"Chelsea gave Fulham, who I thought were quite encouraging, a few chances. They couldn't cope with Josh King.

"I just think that defensively... if Moises Caicedo is back, he'll give them more of a shield, that is for sure. I don't know much about Marco Palestra. I haven't seen him play, so I can't really comment on that one. But I think defensively, they're too vulnerable."

3 Sanchez conceded two and looked nervy throughout the match on Monday Credit: Getty



Clean sheet drought

Maxence Lacroix produced a respectable performance on his competitive debut for the Blues, while Josh Acheampong made several crucial last-ditch interceptions.

However, Levi Colwill seemed out of control on multiple occasions and was lucky Lacroix was covering behind him, suggesting the previous seasons defensive problems still remain as the Blues failed to keep a clean sheet for a 17th consecutive match.

Ally McCoist added: "I think they could beat Arsenal on a one-off. I'm not sure they have the consistency to take them over the 38 games. I think they've got real quality in forward areas. It was a beautiful finish.

"Cole Palmer when he's like that, he's irresistible to watch. He really is. He's just wonderful to watch. They've got brilliant, brilliant players. But I just don't think that consistency wise, you're going to have to maintain a level of consistency over seven, eight months.



"I'm not sure Chelsea will do that. But I think they could beat Arsenal on a one-off, definitely."

Arsenal is THE defensive benchmark

Arsenal enter the campaign defending their crown with an upgraded squad — particularly in defensive areas following the addition of Ezri Konsa.

3 The England international will be most likely a benchwarmer for Arsenal when they have a fully fit squad Credit: Getty

To win the Premier League title, Mikel Arteta made his side the strongest defensively during the previous campaign



They only conceded 27 goals last term, in comparison to Chelsea' who shipped 52.

Additionally, the Gunners' David Raya finished the season with 19 clean sheets in only 37 appearances, and was awarded the Golden Glove award.

Meanwhile, Robert Sanchez managed just nine in 35 outings for the Blues during last term.

Sports.title: What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery... and the club's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi
Sports.content:
What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery... and the club's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Ollie Watkins' absence from the Aston Villa team at Brighton may have been the final chapter in a story that started more than 18 months ago.

The England forward spoke to his team-mates on Monday to explain his side of the story and is now expected to complete his acrimonious move to Al Hilal for around £50million.

Once Watkins had sat out the 4-0 defeat at the Amex, despite being Villa’s only fit striker, it created a rift between the player and the club, not to mention the fans, which was going to take work to heal. But while this row might have been handled differently by both sides, it has not come from a clear blue sky.

Daily Mail Sport looks at how we got here and what life after Watkins might look like...

The Arsenal bid

At some point last week, Watkins had a discussion with Villa manager Unai Emery, who left those talks believing the 30-year-old wanted to move to Al Hilal and was prepared to go to significant lengths to ensure the deal went through.

The striker did not train last week as he waited for Villa to accept a bid. The Saudi Pro League club did not make the required offer and once he understood Watkins would not be involved in the preparation work, Emery did not consider him for the Brighton match. Without the injured Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, strikerless Villa were hammered and Emery did nothing in his media appearances to protect Watkins, who was then targeted by fans online.

Unai Emery was in no mood to protect Ollie Watkins when his star striker was not available for the opening day at Brighton

Al Hilal, whose squad includes former Wolves captain Ruben Neves (furthest right) and Chelsea centre back Kalidou Koulibaly (second right) need to match Villa's £50m valuation

To understand it all, we must rewind to a sliding doors moment for Villa and Watkins — Boxing Day, 2024. In the previous three league games, Emery had picked the chaotic but brilliant Jhon Duran ahead of Watkins and the Colombian scored in all three.

Heading into that match at Newcastle, it looked as though Duran had become Emery’s No 1 striker. Villa knew Arsenal were chasing a forward and had an interest in Watkins, a boyhood Gunners fan.

Then Duran was given a straight red card at Newcastle and when he completed his ban, Emery did not feel his form or attitude merited a return to the team. Al Nassr offered £70m for Duran and Villa decided to cut their losses on a player who was proving difficult to manage.

Villa were unwilling to sell both forwards in the same window and Watkins was denied his dream move to Arsenal, whose offers never hit Villa’s £65m valuation. The forward was disappointed but Emery said: ‘Now we need him, like he needed Aston Villa.’

Emery has lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa this summer and wanted a few senior men to stick with him to build the new era.

Usually, the Spaniard does not stand in a player’s way if he wants to depart, but this one felt more personal.

Contrasting positions

Watkins is the top client at Two Touch, the agency run by former Arsenal youngster Paolo Vernazza. Watkins’ move to Al Hilal would likely be one of Two Touch’s biggest deals and Villa are unhappy with how Vernazza has handled it. Were Vernazza to have his time again, he might do things differently too. Daily Mail Sport has tried to contact the 46-year-old since Sunday, but he has yet to respond.

Jhon Duran was primed to be Villa's No1 striker 18 months ago before a red card at Newcastle

Aston Villa have already lost the likes of Youri Tielemans (left) and Morgan Rogers (right) this summer and Watkins (centre) may be next

Watkins is thought to earn a little more than £100,000-a-week at Villa, yet the salary proposed by Al Hilal is understood to be substantially more. Watkins has also seen Konsa, 28, join Arsenal for roughly the same sum Villa want from Al Hilal. Watkins turns 31 in December and if he believed Villa’s asking price was too high for a player his age, you could understand it. Not surprisingly, Villa saw it differently.

Under Emery, Watkins has developed into one of the best strikers in Europe. The manager has continuously backed him and was rewarded when he hit 12 goals in 13 games at the end of the season to force his way into England’s World Cup squad.

With two forwards injured, Emery needed Watkins at Brighton. No wonder he was ticking before the pre-match interviews. ‘Silence!’ hissed Emery when asked by Sky Sports’ Johnny Phillips about Watkins’ absence. With Emery, the less he says, often the angrier he is.

He looked a man on the edge at the Amex, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual, grew irritable with the opposing bench and stalked down the tunnel at full-time without shaking Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler’s hand. Emery and Hurzeler are not best mates, but the reaction was still telling.

What happens next?

A year ago, it looked as though Emi Martinez had played his final game for Villa. Desperate to move to Manchester United or Atletico Madrid, he was left out for a home defeat by Crystal Palace.

Emery looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual and grew irritable with the opposing bench

Watkins struck 12 goals in the final 13 games of last season to force his way into England's squad for the World Cup, where he scored in the warm-up against Costa Rica

The goalkeeper is still trying to get out, though he knuckled down last season and helped the club win the Europa League. With Watkins, though, that has looked tricky since Sunday.

Whatever the future holds, he has a huge job winning over Villa fans again. The reality is that there were signs last season that Watkins was in decline. A new deal may not have been the best thing for either party.

If Nicolas Jackson comes in, Villa have a striker with potential who can score goals. Emery likes him, having had him at Villarreal. Villa have also made an enquiry to Bayer Leverkusen for 20-year-old striker Christian Kofane. However, at this stage Leverkusen do not wish to sell.

Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they meet Arsenal at Villa Park on Monday.

Sports.title: Raheem Sterling faces two years in jail after being charged with dangerous driving and possessing 'hippy crack' after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini
Sports.content:
Raheem Sterling faces two years in jail after being charged with dangerous driving and possessing 'hippy crack' after crashing his £270,000 Lamborghini

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of laughing gas after his £270,000 Lamborghini crashed in May, it has been reported.

The former Premier League star, 31, who was arrested at the scene of the collision, faces two years in prison if convicted of the charges.

Police were called to the M3 in Hampshire on May 28 to reports of a Lamborghini swerving around the road just before 9am.

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail appeared to show the black luxury 4x4 veering across the three carriageways as other vehicles dodged out of the way.

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon - which is how people ingest laughing gas, also known as 'hippy crack'.

Minutes later, Sterling allegedly crashed the vehicle into the motorway barriers and was cuffed by Hampshire Police.

The force said he would not give a sample after his arrest - leading to a third charge of failing to supply a specimen.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman told The Sun: 'Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

Raheem Sterling has reportedly been charged with dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide, and failing to supply a specimen

Footage obtained by the Daily Mail showed Starling's black Lamborghini M-way scraping the motorway central reservation, minutes before it crashed

The driver appeared to be inhaling from a balloon, just visible as a dark circle above

'The charges come following a single-vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.'

They added that Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court on September 15.

The charges mark a new low for Sterling, who left Chelsea in January after being dropped from their line-up and not playing since May 2024.

In February, he joined Dutch club Feyenoord Rotterdam, but that deal ended in summer and he has been without a club since - despite wanting to play.

The motorist who provided the dashcam footage of Sterling's sports car swerving told the Mail: 'I was in the middle lane and without warning a black Lamborghini pulled in front of me, forcing me to slow.

'I dropped back. I'm a driving instructor after all.

'The car turned back into the inside lane but the driver put his foot down and veered right across all three lanes and seemed to just avoid hitting the central reservation.

'It's a powerful car and he could have easily gone through the central reservation if he'd hit the accelerator.

'A van driver behind him was forced to brake and he then shot off again and turned back across three lanes again into the inside lane.

Sterling is engaged to long-term girlfriend Paige Milian (pictured)

Sterling, here playing for Feyenoord in February, has been without a team since the summer

'This was all caught on dashcam from 8.45am on Thursday. It was just before Junction 4a southbound on the M3.

'The motorist was all over the place but I had no idea it was Raheem Sterling until I saw that he'd been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving by the Minley Interchange.

'I like Raheem but as a driving instructor I'm very concerned.

'He could have easily caused himself - and others - a great deal of harm. He was very fortunate that he did not do so.'

Sterling's representatives declined to comment when contacted by the Daily Mail after the crash, but a source close to the player explained how he had had a hellish two years.

The source said: 'The psychological strain that has been put on him is immeasurable. Isolated. The second he touches a ball, being told he's a flop and he's finished. Mocked. Heckled.

'He moved to the Netherlands to escape and rediscover his love for the game but the negativity followed. It's been an extremely tough couple of years for him and this incident encompasses that.'

Sterling started his career at QPR but broke through at Liverpool as a teenager, before leaving Anfield for Manchester City in 2015, where he won ten major trophies, including the Premier League four times.

He played 82 times for the England senior team, with his last appearance in the 2-1 defeat by France in the quarter-finals of the 2022 World Cup.

However, since leaving City for Chelsea in a £50million deal in 2022 he has endured a torrid spell, which saw him exiled at Stamford Bridge before a failed loan spell with Arsenal and a move to Dutch giants Feyenoord, where he made just eight appearances with no goals.

Sports.title: 'He would have died for Everton': The aching sadness of Mike Lyons, the man who bled blue - and why his story should inspire David Moyes' side to go all out to win this season's League Cup
Sports.content:
A statistic currently going around about Everton being the only club among the Football League's 92 not to have won a trophy, a title or promotion, or been relegated, since the turn of the century has contributed to a pessimism which made a gathering of the club’s faithful last Friday evening very welcome.

The occasion, at the Denbigh Castle pub, a legendary gathering place for Evertonians in central Liverpool, celebrated the former Everton captain Mike Lyons, whose life and career have been charted in a fine new book.

The aching sadness underlying an occasion in which Lyons' former team-mates took turns to relate stories of the indefatigable, generous and hugely talented team-mate they knew and loved, is that the man in question is struggling now and could not be there.

His daughter Francesca, who lives near Liverpool and calls him every day at the care home in Perth, Australia, where he is living with dementia, reminds him how cherished he is among fans. Lyons, 74, knew that the event was taking place and he knows about the book, The Man Who Bled Blue, a meticulously researched and beautifully written biography by the journalist and author Simon Hart. But his brain has frayed terribly. His family and friends have helped Hart piece together the life story.

He would certainly empathise with those 21st century fans who yearn for silverware – any silverware – and not least the League Cup, which sends the team to Preston, David Moyes’ old club, on Wednesday night. Everton were reigning English champions, four days away from contesting a European Cup quarter-final, when Lyons made his debut in March 1971.

Mick Lyons made 473 appearances for Everton in his 12 years on Merseyside, scoring 59 goals

‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses’

With Everton team-mates Martin Dobson (left) and Bob Latchford (right)

Yet his 11 years as an Everton player did not yield him a single honour. Liverpool won 15 in that time. By 1982, Lyons was on his way to Sheffield Wednesday, missing by a couple of years the start of the glorious era when Everton won the FA Cup and two titles.

Had Lyons been at Friday’s event, talk would inevitably have turned to the League Cup – and his huge role in Everton's marathon against Aston Villa in the 1977 final, won by Villa in a second replay at Old Trafford. It remains one of the greatest clashes in the tournament's history and was the closest Lyons ever came to silverware with Everton.

Evertonians still remember the intensity of his celebration when he scored an equaliser in front of the Stretford End in the second replay. ‘Michael was more animated there than at any other goal he scored,’ his brother, Joe, tells Hart in the book. (To his family, Lyons has always been ‘Michael.’) Fatefully, he was then asked to push up as a utility centre-forward as Everton chased a winner – it’s a strategy still known as ‘Doing a Mike Lyons’ among Evertonians – and a hole materialised at the back which Villa exploited to score a late winner. In the seclusion of the car on the way home, Lyons wept.

This story teaches us, among other things, that barren times can produce some of the greatest heroes, like Lyons, and that the League Cup can bring such indelible memories that Everton, who have not always fielded strong teams in recent times, should see it as an opportunity.

Hart relates how, despite the initial Wembley final not yielding a winner, the team still appeared on a planned open-bus tour of Liverpool for which vast crowds turned out. The first replay, a thrilling 1-1 draw in Sheffield rescued by a late Bob Latchford goal, would remain one of Lyons’ favourite nights of his career. He later described the noise made by Evertonians that night as ‘something I’ll always treasure. It embodied everything I’ve always felt for this club’.

The biography’s title, alongside an image of Lyons with a gashed face as he leaves the pitch after Everton’s 1980 FA Cup semi-final against West Ham – another one they lost – captures his contribution. His myriad cuts, blows and collisions form a backdrop to the book. ‘He would have died for Everton,’ said his manager Gordon Lee, who declared he wanted ‘Eleven Mike Lyonses.’

The book’s beauty also resides in its small details, capturing the boundless enthusiasm and often comic innocence which accompanied Lyons huge professionalism and work ethic.

He drove a club-issue Lada with his name emblazoned down the side. He eschewed the posh Liverpool hair salon which the players attended for their curly perms in favour of the work of team-mate Roger Kenyon’s wife Jackie, a hairdresser. Mrs Kenyon and Lyons’ wife Tricia were in such deep conversation in the Lyons’ kitchen that the perm solution was left in the Everton captain’s hair for too long. It was a catastrophe.

Shaking hands with Liverpool captain Emlyn Hughes ahead of the 1977 FA Cup semi-final at Maine Road

It is now 31 years since Everton last lifted a trophy, the 1995 FA Cup

The League Cup is the only major domestic trophy that Everton have never won, and it is time they rectified that point

You could have heard a pin drop in that Liverpool pub on Friday night when Francesca Lyons told the 100 or so people gathered that her father would have been humbled by all this attention. The consequences of his repeated heading of the ball are the same that so many old pros have had to face, full on, and Francesca has been an impressive advocate for football's need to do more for them.

There is a reason why the book’s subtitle is The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons. The Villa captain in the 1977 final was Chris Nicholl, who lived with the form of dementia caused by repeatedly heading footballs during his playing career, before he passed away in 2024.

But Friday evening was about the life-affirming qualities of a captain and player who, Francesca insisted, would not have had his life any other way. ‘He has always been so upbeat and fun,’ she said. ‘He would have probably laughed off all the attention because he’s always been so humble.’

Moyes, who also loves the bones of Everton, has a deep understanding of Lyons’ contribution. He and his long-time assistant Billy McKinlay paid him a visit during an Everton pre-season tour of Australia some time back. The League Cup remains a trophy Everton have never won. Lyons, who still watches the club’s games from Perth, would smile to see them finally lift the three-handled trophy next March, 50 years on from that legendary three-game marathon against Villa.

The Man Who Bled Blue: The Triumphs and Tragedy of Mike Lyons by Simon Hart is published by Mount Vernon Publishing.

Sports.title: LASK 5 CELTIC 1: Bhoys' Euro dream turns into a nightmare as Austrians let rip with five goals without reply
Sports.content:
LASK 5 CELTIC 1: Bhoys' Euro dream turns into a nightmare as Austrians let rip with five goals without reply

Austrians reach Champions League at Celtic's expense after 5-4 aggregate win

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Since embarking on their maiden European voyage in the old Inter-City Fairs Cup some 64 years ago, Celtic have scaled some dizzying heights and experienced some crushing lows.

Perhaps never before has the sense of sheer desolation felt quite as acute as it did when the final whistle signal sounded last night in northern Austria.

On an occasion when Martin O'Neill's side simply wilted before your eyes, a return ticket to the big stage was ripped up and the accompanying £40million in prize money slipped through the club's hands.

It was a catastrophic outcome – one which beggared belief after such a commanding display in Glasgow six days previously.

How could a side which was in such complete control of a tie at the midway point look so ramshackle and lost?

Celtic players are dejected in Austria as their Champions League bid disintegrates

It's much too easy to cite complacency on the players' part as the reason why Celtic again crashed out at this stage. They didn't initially play like a team that already believed the job was done. They just stopped playing.

Not since collapsing away to MTK Hungarian in 1963-64 had Celtic surrendered a three-goal first leg lead. The fallout from this will be nuclear.

For all the board were given some credit for lavishing £30million on four players, two of those – Mika Baur and Haissem Hassan – arrived too late in the window to take this match in their stride.

And where are the others which O'Neill evidently needed in the door sooner? The left-back, the holding midfielder that European football demands, the additional creative influence?

A club that's still in profit for this window didn't get its act together in good time. And, accordingly, it won't be returning to the big stage.

And so, the name of LASK joins that of AEK Athens, Cluj, Ferencvaros, Midtjylland, Kairat Almaty as sides to have knocked Celtic out in Champions League qualification in recent times.

You could lose one of those ties, maybe two, even if you are going about things the right way. When you chalk up six losses on the spin, you aren't behaving like a serious football club.

Few who watched this debacle unfold will ever have seen anything like it. It was scarcely believable.

When Callum McGregor found the net in 21 minutes, Celtic were four goals up on aggregate and contemplating what Thursday's draw in Monaco might bring.

While Benjamin Nygren's error allowed Moses Usor to level on the night before the break, there was no need to panic.

But that's exactly what unfolded. Auston Trusty's error played a part in Robert Ljubicic cutting the aggregate deficit to two.

Camilo Duran looks pained as Celtic suffer in Austria

More untidy defending then saw Samuel Adeniran net LASK's third and at that point Celtic were running about with their hair on fire.

With the Austrians completely dominant and managing 31 attempts in regulation time, the only wonder was that it took them until the 90th minute to square the tie with substitute Florian Flecker heading home a rebound.

Adeniran sealed an extraordinary comeback in extra-time following another elementary error and even had the luxury of having a penalty saved.

Celtic actually started the game fairly well. Baur's cross had a little too much on it for Kasper Hogh.

The German's interception sent Hogh in on goal. A poor execution ensured the keeper saved comfortably.

LASK were not shy at trying their luck from distance or shelling the box with crosses.

They were left with their heads in their hands when Xavier Mbuyamba failed to convert at the back post following a flick-on.

O'Neill's heart would have skipped a beat when Melayro Bogarde's strike took a deflection off McGregor and bounced off the upright.

Arriving just before the midway point in the first half, Celtic's opener owed everything to their pace and invention down the left flank.

Hyun-jun Yang played the ball back to Kieran Tierney and darted forward. Having taken the return ball, he bobbed and weaved while assessing his options.

LASK's Samuel Adeniran celebrates scoring his team's fifth goal against Celtic

Having correctly identified that McGregor was best placed to capitalise, he cut the ball back. The skipper's left-foot strike came off the outstretched leg of Andres Andrade and beat Lukas Jungwirth in goal.

Hogh looked like removing any lingering doubt soon after only for a nudge in his back to put him off.

With LASK looking increasingly frustrated, Adeniran pulled a shot wide of the far post then left one on Colby Donovan.

Celtic should have been coasting at half-time. Instead, LASK gave them something to worry about.

There was nothing wrong with Cameron Carter-Vickers' pass to Nygren. The Swede went blind with his attempted pass back.

Moses Usor could hardly believe his luck. A calm first-time finish gave the Austrians hope.

For O'Neill's players, it was a question of staying disciplined and sticking to their respective tasks at the outset of the second period.

Yet within three minutes, Trusty got himself done for pace and power on the left. LASK moved the ball into the central Robert Ljubicic.

The playmaker's shot from the edge of the box did fly through a thicket of legs. Still, Sinisalo was too easily beaten.

Ten minutes later, the unthinkable inched ever closer. A long punt up the park found Celtic's defence disjointed.

Donovan gave Ljubicic too much space to pick a pass to Adeniran. To that point in the tie, the American had played like his laces had been tied together. Not this time. His cushioned left-foot strike curled away from the outstretched arm of Sinisalo. Celtic were in trouble.

Reo Hatate and Seb Tounekti were introduced before Luke McCowan and Liam Scales joined them. Dane Murray later replaced the stricken Donovan.

Sinisalo did well to turn Sascha Horvath's deflected strike wide then watched Joao Viktor Tornich's point blank header flash wide.

When Adeniran's strike thumped the underside of the bar, the ball hit Sinisalo's back but stayed out. Celtic were riding their luck.

Celtic players call for offside after Florian Flecker's goal for LASK

O'Neill picked up a booking for venting his growing frustrations at the officials. Of greater concern was Kasper Jorgensen's shot which flew narrowly wide. Celtic were handing the ball as if it was a hot potato.

The clock had just struck 90 minutes when they conceded again. Finding himself in acres of space on the left, George Bello crossed. Sinisalo did brilliantly to prevent an initial header from finding the net but could do nothing as sub Florian Flecker nodded home the rebound.

All the momentum was with the Austrians in extra-time. Celtic got through the first period only to concede a fifth four minutes after the turnaround.

McCowan became the latest visiting player to make an enforced error when he won the ball on the edge of his own box and had his pocket picked. The ball was worked to Adeniran at the edge of the box who beat Sinisalo all too easily.

The Finn kept Celtic breathing by saving Adeniran's penalty after Hatate had felled Krystof Danek. It only prolonged the agony.

Sports.title: Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... United youngster linked with Feyenoord Manchester United forward Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Feyenoord. The Dutch side, coached by Giovanni van Bronckhorst, want cover in case they lose a forward in the final stages of the window. Obi Martin, a Denmark U21 international, had interest from Cologne earlier in the window. Feyenoord would also offer Champions League football. Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Dutch side Feyenoord Forest close in on Delap deal Nottingham Forest and Chelsea are closing on a £45million deal for Liam Delap. Talks intensified on Monday following Chelsea's game at Fulham and a verbal agreement is in place for the 23-year-old to link up with Oliver Glasner's team. He is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours. Liam Delap is expected to undergo a Nottingham Forest medical in the next 24 hours United complete Baleba deal Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal. ‘I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level,' said the 22-year-old, who has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford. ‘The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.’ For more on this story click HERE Carlos Baleba with Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox Gonzalez says goodbye to City ahead of £50m Newcastle move Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez is travelling to the North East to finalise his £50m move to Newcastle United. The 24-year-old Spaniard will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours. Gonzalez said his farewells to City team-mates this morning and the deal is set to be £47m plus £3m in add-ons. Nico Gonzalez will become Newcastle United's latest signing of the summer City defender Kabore set for Wrexham medical Manchester City defender Issa Kabore is due for a medical at Wrexham after they agreed a £2million fee. The 25-year-old spent last season on loan at Wrexham and wants to continue with the club as they attempt to take the next step up to the Premier League. Kabore, who has 55 caps for Burkina Faso, has had eight loan spells since joining City from Mechelen in 2020. Ipswich Town want £9m for Wrexham target Anis Mehmeti and Birmingham City are also interested. Issa Kabore, pictured while on loan at Luton in 2024, is set to move to Wrexham Bees still buzzing about Diouf Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season. West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre. The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league. AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him . Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City. They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah. Forest have also opened talks with Celta Vigo for right-back Javi Rueda. Forest are discussing an £8m offer for the 25-year-old who joined Celta from Real Madrid in 2024. Villa enquire over Kofane Aston Villa have made an enquiry to Bayer Leverkusen for striker Christian Kofane. As well as working on Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, Villa want another forward. As Daily Mail Sport revealed, they were rebuffed in an enquiry for Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta but have now turned to Kofane. The 20-year-old's agent was in England earlier this summer talking to the likes of Everton and Arsenal. However, at this stage Leverkusen do not wish to sell. Wrexham close on £8m move Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push. Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million. Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers. Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old. Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m. They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti. NATHAN SALT Olympiacos in for Edson Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan. The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far. Doncaster living the life O'Reilly Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan. A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe. Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season Tottenham seal Savinho deal Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho. Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons. Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City. Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world. 'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.' De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity. 'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.' Savinho signs on the dotted line for his move to Spurs Pinnock in for Coventry medical Ethan Pinnock is due to have his medical at Coventry today ahead of singing a three-year contract with an option to extend. The promoted club agreed a £6m fee with Brentford for the 33-year-old defender yesterday. Ethan Pinnock is set to bolster Frank Lampard's squad at Coventry Chelsea in talks over Guiu exit Napoli are continuing talks with Chelsea for Marc Guiu and defender Mamadou Sarr’s proposed loan to Sociedad is progressing. Chelsea have asked about Atalanta defensive prospect Honest Anahor. Villa look at Leao deal Aston Villa are exploring the finances of a deal for AC Milan's Rafael Leao. Daily Mail Sport reported last night that the club had made contact over the winger, 27. Turkish giants Galatasaray remain in the mix for the Portuguese as well. Rafael Leao in pre-season action against Chelsea Bakwa off to Lille Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa is joining Lille on loan. The 23-year-old signed for Forest from Strasbourg last September in a deal worth £30million but has failed to have the desired impact. He is due for a medical today and will play in the Champions League with Lille. Dilane Bakwa is set to leave after just one season at the City Ground City set to go back to Enzo Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez. The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet. But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night. Sports.title: Leeds do the double over Nottingham Forest: Daniel Farke's side win at the City Ground for the second time in just FOUR days with Carabao Cup triumph - and Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for new boss Oliver Glasner
Sports.content:
Leeds do the double over Nottingham Forest: Daniel Farke's side win at the City Ground for the second time in just FOUR days with Carabao Cup triumph - and Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for new boss Oliver Glasner

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liam Delap cannot come quickly enough for Nottingham Forest. Two games into Oliver Glasner’s reign at the City Ground, two defeats to Leeds United, and zero goals. He started three strikers and they still couldn’t score.

And, so, for the second time in four days, Daniel Farke’s team came to town and took full advantage of a team still trying to find their new identity. First for three points on Saturday, now for a place in the League Cup third round.

Daniel James was afforded the freedom of West Bridgford all evening and fittingly gave Leeds the lead before James Justin bundled in a second after a long throw caused chaos in the Forest box.

Glasner’s side, once again, looked in desperate need of new blood. Thankfully, news emerged a few hours before kick-off that Forest had agreed a club-record fee of £45million, potentially rising to £50m, for the Chelsea striker. A remarkable whack for a player who scored just one Premier League goal last season and wasn’t even training with the first-team.

Daniel James scored the opening goal as Leeds United won 2-0 at Nottingham Forest

James Justin (right) scored the second as Leeds knocked Forest out of the Carabao Cup

Delap is by no means the first budding talent to be chewed up and spat out by Chelsea and if Glasner can unleash the old-fashioned centre-forward that thrived at Ipswich, he would be just what they need. Glasner likes a physical focal point, as he had at Palace in Jean-Philippe Mateta, to hold it all together and bring team-mates around him into play as those around him attack with pace.

‘A frustrating night,’ said Glasner, who refused to comment on Delap’s impending arrival. ‘Last season told everyone what is needed, not just tonight. Nine months of relegation battle, losing maybe your top midfielder and now just six weeks together. The reality is no magician, no messiah, just hard work.’

That’s why Forest still look better when Chris Wood leading the line but he’s 35 in December and struggles with injury. He had the best chances of the night for Forest but couldn’t take any of them. A sensational last-ditch tackle from Joe Rodon denied him after a neat nutmeg of Nico Elvedi left him with just James Trafford to beat. Wood had another fine chance in the second half, too, but couldn’t beat Trafford from eight yards.

Trafford is quickly starting to enjoy his football again. Two matches since his £40m move from Manchester City and two clean sheets.

‘It was a remarkable level of performance,’ said Leeds boss Farke. ‘Never in doubt, it was a fully deserved win. I saw how dominant we can be against really good sides.’

Forest boss Oliver Glasner has plenty to mull over after starting his reign with two defeats

Carabao Cup R2 results: August 25 Cardiff City 1-2 Norwich City Doncaster Rovers 1-3 Middlesbrough Barnsley 3-2 Crewe Alexandra Blackburn Rovers 1-2 Sheffield United Blackpool 1-4 Lincoln City Cambridge United 0-1 Millwall Fletwood Town 4-0 Shrewsbury Town Ipswich Town 3-1 Leicester City Plymouth Argyle 2-4 Coventry City Sheffield Wednesday 0-2 Wolverhampton Wanderers Southampton 1-4 West Ham United Stevenage 0-3 Reading Stoke City 1-1 Hull City* (4-5 on penalties) Walsall 0-0 Leyton Orient* (5-6 on penalties) Watford 1-5 Peterborough Town Birmingham City 1-6 Brentford Nottingham Forest 0-2 Leeds United

Forest, meanwhile, are still getting used to playing Glasner’s way and James repeatedly exploited the space behind wing-back Williams. James whipped one cross in to set up a glorious chance for Sean Longstaff, saw a shot of his own saved by Matz Sels.

On 50 minutes, Williams bombed forward only for Arnaud Kalimuemdo to give the ball away and leave Forest exposed. Longstaff slipped in James who fired past Sels before Williams could get back.

The puzzle of how to replace Elliot Anderson remains unsolved.

Leeds’ second summed it all up as the ball bounced its way to the back post, Williams tried to clear it but couldn’t, almost put it into his own net, only for Justin and Lucas Nmecha to finally help it in.

At least it was a more entertaining spectacle than four days ago. Neither side deserved to win that one. Leeds warranted every bit of their victory this time. The boos at full-time told you that.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year after record-breaking season for Man United... and he's one of just TWO stars outside Arsenal and Man City in the Team of the Year
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes has been named the PFA Players' Player of the Year after a landmark 2025-26 campaign in which the Manchester United captain broke the Premier League record for most assists in a single season.

Fernandes surpassed the previous mark of 20, jointly held by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, on the final day of the season when he set up Patrick Dorgu's header against Brighton to register his 21st assist of the campaign.

Fernandes has already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick by collecting the prestigious, player-voted award at Manchester's Opera House on Tuesday evening.

He was United's first to claim the PFA Players' Player of the Year since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

'Winning this, being voted by the ones that every week go out on the pitch against me, is something that makes me very proud,' he said.

'Because they've been there, they're playing against me, they've seen what I'm capable of doing, and for them to vote for me is something I'm very grateful for.

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was crowned PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday

Fernandes, who attended with his wife Ana, was also named in the PFA Team of the Year

Fernandes had already won the Premier League Player of the Season and the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year accolades, and completed the hat-trick on Tuesday evening

'It's always nice to see the name of the club in these kinds of awards, and obviously the players stand out with the club behind them. That's very important for us.

'I hope that from now on we can have even more players from our club having this kind of recognition, because it's also important and means that we're doing something very good.

'Individually, you want to have these accolades to show that your game is helping the team and that there are a lot of good things you've been doing to help them.'

The Portugal midfielder was the sole United player to have been named in the PFA's Premier League Team of the Year, and he is joined by Brentford's Igor Thiago as the only other non-Manchester City or Arsenal player in the side.

David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice all made up a heavily defensive Arsenal contingent, while Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland completed City's representation.

Mohamed Salah was named PFA Players' Player of the Year last year, but no Liverpool players made the cut this time.

O'Reilly also scooped the Men's Young Player of the Year award, beating team-mate Cherki as well as Max Dowman, Junior Kroupi, Kobbie Mainoo and Rio Ngumoha to the prize.

Elsewhere, Everton's Hayden Hackney was named the Championship Player of the Year after playing a key role in Middlesbrough's run to the play-off final in May. He signed for David Moyes' side in July after missing out on promotion with his boyhood club.

Nico O'Reilly (left) won the PFA Young Player, while Declan Rice was in the Team of the Year

Dom Ballard took home the League One title after a standout season for Leyton Orient while Swindon's Aaron Drinan won the League Two award.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award for the second time after also collecting it in 2024, becoming only the third player to win it twice after Lucy Bronze (2014 and 2017) and Fran Kirby (2018 and 2021).

Shaw was the WSL's Golden Boot winner last season, scoring 21 goals in 22 matches as she helped fire her team to the top-flight trophy for the first time in 10 years.

The other nominees for the top prize in the women's game were Manchester City team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Chelsea's Lauren James, Manchester United's Jess Park, Arsenal's Alessia Russo and Aston Villa's Kirsty Hanson.

Manchester City's Bunny Shaw lifted the Women's Players' Player of the Year award

Arsenal's Olivia Smith scooped the Young Player of the Year award after a fine season

PREMIER LEAGUE AND WSL TEAMS OF THE YEAR Premier League team of the year: David Raya (Arsenal); Jurrien Timber (Arsenal), William Saliba (Arsenal), Gabriel Magalhaes (Arsenal), Nico O'Reilly (Man City); Bruno Fernandes (Man United), Declan Rice (Arsenal), Rayan Cherki (Man City); Erling Haaland (Man City), Antoine Semenyo (Man City), Igor Thiago (Brentford). WSL team of the year: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea); Kerstin Casparij (Man City), Toko Koga (Tottenham), Ellie Carpenter (Chelsea), Emily Fox (Arsenal); Yui Hasegawa (Man City), Mariona Caldentey (Arsenal), Jess Park (Man United); Bunny Shaw (Man City), Alessia Russo (Arsenal), Lauren James (Chelsea).

Hannah Hampton, Kerstin Casparij, Toko Koga, Ellie Carpenter and Emily Fox made up the remainder of the PFA WSL Team of the Year.

Arsenal's Olivia Smith, the former most expensive transfer in women's history, scooped the Young Player of the Year award.

The 22-year-old Canada international became the first women's player to surpass the seven-figure barrier last summer when Arsenal signed her from Liverpool for £1 million, and had an impressive campaign, scoring five goals and recording three assists.

Sports.title: Serena Williams makes spectacular return to US Open as she teams up with Carlos Alcaraz in mixed power pairing... four years after stepping back from tennis at the Grand Slam
Sports.content:
Serena Williams made an emotional return to Flushing Meadows on Tuesday when she teamed up with Spanish sensation Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open's mixed doubles event.

The tennis icon, 44, continued her comeback tour, returning to the Grand Slam where she bowed out of the sport four years ago.

Williams announced that she would be 'evolving away' from tennis following the 2022 US Open. But, after returning to tennis's major stages at Wimbledon and the Cincinnati Open earlier this year, she stepped into the spotlight on Arthur Ashe once again.

The US Tennis Association announced on Saturday that Williams and Alcaraz, 23, had been handed a wild card for the year's final Grand Slam.

The pair were granted entry into the star-studded 16-team field competing for a $1million prize, sealing a stunning return to the US Open for Williams.

They took to the iconic Arthur Ashe court on Tuesday afternoon, facing Lloyd Glasspool and Erin Routliffe in the first round of the event.

Serena Williams made an emotional return to the US Open in the mixed doubles on Tuesday

The 44-year-old teamed up with Spanish ace Carlos Alcaraz (pictured) in the event

The tennis legend stepped back from the sport following the 2022 US Open

It will be the 44-year-old's first time playing at the US Open since 2022. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion returned to tennis earlier this summer.

But she is not planning to play singles in New York. The USTA had been holding one women's wild card - presumably in case Williams wanted it. On Saturday, however, organizers announced it had gone to American Sofia Kenin , the 2020 Australian Open champion.

Williams played singles at Wimbledon, losing in the first round and sustaining a knee injury, before teaming up with older sister Venus to play doubles at the Cincinnati Open. In their first match together since the 2022 US Open, the sisters were beaten by Peyton Stearns and Marta Kostyuk, 6-2, 1-6, 10-8.

Serena Williams has won a US Open mixed doubles title before, taking the crown in 1998 alongside Max Mirnyi, who now works with Aryna Sabalenka . Nearly three decades on, the competition is now a star-studded, two-day competition, with Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic among the other big names taking part this year.

Alcaraz, meanwhile, announced this week he would return to defend his US Open singles title after being sidelined since April with a right wrist injury.

News of his comeback - and his partnership with Williams - is a huge boost for fans after rival Jannik Sinner pulled out.

The world No 1 announced on Friday that he will miss the US Open with a knee injury.

In a statement on social media, the Italian wrote: 'Even though I have been working hard with my team and my medical staff, we have now had to make the difficult decision that I will not be able to compete at the US Open this year.

Serena Williams was world No.1 in singles the day Carlos Alcaraz was born.



23 years later, the two join forces in Grand Slam mixed doubles! pic.twitter.com/MvUSxZXlyf — US Open Tennis (@usopen) August 25, 2026

The tennis icon continued her comeback tour, returning to the Grand Slam in New York

Serena Williams' Wimbledon singles comeback came to an early end on Tuesday

The legend was supported by her husband Alexis Ohanian and their two daughters

'We have been back on court in Monte Carlo over the last couple of days and have realised that I still need more time to recover from my right knee issue.

'I'm obviously very sad and disappointed, as New York has a special place in my heart. I was very much looking forward to coming back and playing in the electric atmosphere in front of the great fans there.'

Sinner turned pro in 2018 and has never missed a Grand Slam tournament in his entire career, winning five in total - including the US Open two years ago and Wimbledon this summer.

The 25-year-old has been dominant so far in 2026, winning the first five ATP Masters 1000 events, two of which in the US in Indian Wells and Miami.

After crashing out of Wimbledon in the first round and suffering a similar fate alongside sister Venus in the women's doubles in Cincinnati, many have questioned if Williams still possesses her titan talent.

Others may be more focused on the question mark over one particular detail of her preparation -whether Williams has continued to use GLP-1 jabs managed by telehealth company Ro, of which she became a vocal paid spokesperson for last year.

Williams returned to tennis this summer and played with sister Venus at the Cincinnati Open

The seven-time Wimbledon champion's husband Alexis Ohanian sits on the company's board and was an early investor. As recently as this February Williams, the company's celebrity face, featured in a Super Bowl advert for the brand and its Zepbound tirzepatide jab, which is also marketed under the name Mounjaro.

Williams, who is said to have lost close to two and a half stone, or 34 pounds (15kg) using the drug, previously called her challenge to lose weight following the birth of her two children 'the one opponent (she) couldn't beat'.

It remains unclear as to whether Williams has continued to use the drug, which also treats symptoms of diabetes, with her publicist declining to comment when asked by the Atlantic.

But although GLP-1s are not banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), they are one of the drugs under ongoing investigation as to whether they might be classed as performance-enhancing in the future.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
